Hearts of iron is like a typical paradox franchise except the focus of the game is war. If you ever played one of the other paradox games and wished that it had more depth in the military aspects of the game then HOI is for you. I feel like it doesn't have as much replayability as the other games because once you learn the optimum military strategy for a country given it's strategic position and the resources available to it then it's like you beat the game.

Paradox has made effort to give it more replayability by making opportunities to pursue ahistorical scenarios or to play as countries that were not major players in the war, but it doesn't really work out. If you want to play as a minor country then your resources and production are so low that your military will not be able to meaningfully contribute. If you want ahistorical scenarios like "UK becomes fascist and joins the axis" it will throw off the competitive balance of the war so much and the AI won't be able to compensate enough to make it fun.

After playing HoI4 so much, my favorite thing to do in it has become just making alt history or historical scenario maps with the console.

It's a decent strategy game and, despite the usual kiked portrayal of the Second World War, it's unintentionally based due to no mention whatsoever of the holocaust.

If you're a fan of Star Wars, consider Shadows of the Empire. It's a classic for me.
